title: Profiling and posture in ISE
domain: Secure Network Access, Visibility, and Enforcement
blurb: Let ISE work out what each device is, and check that laptops are healthy before granting full access.
purpose: Knowing who someone is isn't enough; you also need to know what the device is and whether it's healthy. This lab sets up ISE profiling and posture checks to grant access based on device type and compliance. It covers advanced ISE features.
scenario: Printers and IP phones should be recognized automatically, and corporate laptops should get full access only if their antivirus is running and the disk is encrypted. Turn on profiling probes in ISE, and build a posture policy with remediation.
topology:
Endpoints ── SW1 ── ISE (PSN: profiling, posture)
                    Secure Client with ISE Posture module
objectives: Choose the profiling probes and how data reaches ISE
Put the posture flow in order
Write posture requirements and authorization rules by compliance

steps.title: Profiling probes
steps.learn: **Profiling** classifies endpoints from the attributes they reveal. The best sources are **RADIUS** (MAC address and OUI), **DHCP** (hostname and vendor class), **HTTP** (user agent), **SNMP** queries of the switch, and **Device Sensor** on the switch, which packs CDP, LLDP and DHCP data into RADIUS accounting.
steps.task: Match each probe to the data it gives ISE.
steps.screen: ISE › Administration › System › Deployment › PSN › Profiling Configuration

steps.title: The posture flow
steps.learn: A posture check runs after authentication. Until the result is in, the endpoint gets limited access, and **Change of Authorization (CoA)** updates its access once the result is known.
steps.question: Order from login to full access.
items: The laptop authenticates with 802.1X, and its posture status is Unknown
ISE returns a limited authorization (redirect ACL to the posture portal)
The Secure Client posture module checks the requirements and reports to ISE
ISE sends a RADIUS CoA, and the switch reauthenticates the session with full access

steps.title: Posture requirements
steps.learn: A **requirement** pairs **conditions** with a **remediation**. Mandatory requirements must pass for the device to be compliant. Optional ones only warn.
steps.task: Make antivirus **mandatory** with an **AV definition update** remediation, and disk encryption **mandatory** with a **message** remediation telling the user to call the help desk.
steps.screen: ISE › Work Centers › Posture › Posture Policy

steps.title: Authorize by compliance
steps.learn: Authorization rules can use **Session:PostureStatus**. Order them so compliant devices get full access, unknown devices are redirected to posture, and non-compliant devices get a remediation-only network.
steps.task: Give each posture status its authorization profile.
steps.screen: ISE › Policy Sets › Wired-Access › Authorization Policy

steps.title: Why CoA matters
steps.question: Without RADIUS CoA, what would happen when a laptop becomes compliant?

options.text: It would stay in the limited redirect session until it reauthenticated on its own, for example after a reconnect or session timeout, because the switch wouldn't know the result had changed.
It would get full access immediately anyway.
options.why: The switch enforces whatever ISE last told it. CoA is how ISE changes that mid-session.

options.text: ISE would drop the laptop's session.
options.why: Without CoA, ISE can't act on the session at all.

summary: Profiling probes and the data each provides, the posture flow with CoA, mandatory antivirus and encryption requirements with remediation, and authorization rules by posture status.
